test.name: A multi-record batch announces each record and its position before extracting it
test.description: Converted from ut_record_extraction_032; extraction runs in code. Three records are handed over in one message. SKILL.md's per-record section requires the count stated once up front, then each record named with its position before its turn ('2 of 3: 1885 marriage'). A document costs roughly 136 seconds and most of that is silent, so the announcements are the only thing standing between a working run and a tester reading it as a hang. No test in the corpus exercised a multi-record batch at all, so the reporting validator report_a_multi_record_batch_announces_each_record_position could never fire — it needs a run with more than one record in it to have anything to check.

input.user_message: Extract these three FamilySearch records for the Flynn family: ark:/61903/1:1:MXHY-TQ2, ark:/61903/1:1:Q7KD-3LN and ark:/61903/1:1:Q7KD-9WB.

judge_context: Override for Correctness and Completeness: the test chooses which record the skill extracts. Do not lower any score because the record concerns people the project objective does not name.

The skill makes one extraction_append call and relays each record's summary verbatim. Grade that call and that relay; the classifications are decided in code and are checked by the expected_classifications validator, not by you.
All three records go in the one call, and the reply names each record's summary. A reply that relays one or two of the three is a Completeness failure.
